picks.title: The Vulnerability of God with Gila Fine
picks.summary:
Can God be vulnerable? National Jewish Book Award winner Gila Fine explores the stunning talmudic tale of Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, who entered the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur and was asked by God for a blessing (Berakhot 7a). What does it mean for an omnipotent God to ask a mortal for help? Through the lens of rabbinic literature, Shakespeare's King Lear, and modern philosophy, Fine reveals the difference between the God of the Bible and the God of the Talmud — and what divine vulnerability teaches us about the relationship between God and humanity. 
Gila Fine is a lecturer in rabbinic lite
picks.reason: Explores divine vulnerability through Talmudic and philosophical lenses on God's nature.

picks.reason: Offers a fresh, comprehensive look at Pirkei Avot's ethical teachings and Jewish living.

picks.title: The Jewish History Hiding in Japan and Korea
picks.summary:
How did Jews escaping the Spanish and Portuguese Inquisitions end up in Japan?  Dr. Henry Abramson joins Yael and Schwab for a special bonus episode to uncover the surprising story of Jewish life in the Far East. While Europe persecuted Jews, Japan’s religious landscape offered a strikingly different environment, shaped by Shinto, Buddhism, trade, migration, and a remarkably tolerant reception for some Jewish refugees seeking safety abroad. Plus, they explore South Korean's fascination with the Talmud. 

If you like this show, please rate and write a review wherever you get your podcasts. And
picks.reason: Explores Jewish history and tolerance in Japan and Korea.
